coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every mapped test in scripts/suite-m{2,3,4,5,6,8}.mjs and the inline M1 block of scripts/acceptance.mjs was read against its assertion's observable; each of the 51 suite-required mappings across the seven executed milestones names a test that genuinely exercises the clause. Spot-checked in depth: m3-a11 does not merely click the quote preview, it waits on #message-<originalId> and then on a getBoundingClientRect predicate proving the target scrolled into the viewport; m3-a15 compares a full SELECT id FROM messages snapshot before and after re-running every installed starter segment; m2-a24 reads two pages of both feeds and asserts set-cardinality equals row count plus presence of all 25 freshly written ids; m8-a01 recomputes all six lifetime totals from independent SQL over the stored corpus and then re-asserts them against the rendered sm-insights-total-* nodes; m6-a13 shells out to the frozen instrument validator and the lane's own sample verifier and requires verification.json.pass. scripts/acceptance.mjs derives the required id list from the frozen manifest itself and asserts coverage for every suite-required id before declaring a pass, so an unmapped assertion cannot yield a green suite. No mapping was found to point at a test that does not exercise its observable.

defects.summary: The M6 acceptance suite silently requires a separately-launched push worker. Run from a documented cold start without `node scripts/push-worker.mjs` already running, the push-payload test fails on an assert whose message is the 115-character padded probe body, giving no indication that the provider process is simply absent.

Two frozen mid-curve degradation rules fail at the 50% checkpoint of the lane's own scale replay: global message search p95 16.33 ms against a 15.19 ms interpolated ceiling, and Insights p95 5.01 ms against 4.26 ms. The lane's own envelope script records allBuilderChecksPass:false. Growth is superlinear mid-curve even though both full-corpus 3x ratios pass.

A non-member's chat.apiHistory read of a conversation returns a successful empty page (data: [], no denial) rather than an authorization refusal. No data leaks, but a client cannot distinguish 'chat you may not read' from 'chat with no messages', unlike the mutation paths which return NOT_MEMBER / NOT_FOUND.

posts.removed is declared in snapback/schema.q with a default and is read by every feed and Insights projection, but no mutation in the generated API can ever set it, so the flag is unreachable dead surface. (The brief does not require post deletion, so nothing in the checklist is affected.)
defects.evidence: snapback/schema.q:37 and :83; snapback/generated/api.ts has no post-removal mutation; grading/trace.md#defect-d-05

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), interpolated toward 90 but held well short of it by the missing platform proofs.
O1.justification: 101 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent execution (M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18). M1-M5 are not merely solid but complete - 79/79, with every suite re-run green in this session and every choreography receipt passing. That is materially past the 60 anchor. The 90 anchor is not reachable: it names platform-proof artifacts explicitly, and all nine native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07, m8-a17, m8-a18) have no scoreable proof - both simulator statuses are recorded 'not-recorded'. M7's nine assertions also score not passed, since the environment overlay makes M7 a separate later session while the full-run denominator still counts it. The shortfall is entirely concentrated in those two blocks; nothing in the executed scope is patchy.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), placed close to 90.
O2.justification: An adversarial sweep beyond the checklist produced no crashes, no wrong data and no broken flows. Retrying a write with the same id did not duplicate it; self-follow was refused with CANNOT_FOLLOW_SELF and left both counts unchanged; editing a tombstone was refused with MESSAGE_DELETED and the tombstone held; three concurrent reactions from one user collapsed to exactly one; five pages of history returned 100 unique rows with zero duplicates; search honoured case-insensitive word-prefix, rejected mid-word, and matched across NFC and NFD; a 6-character password was refused with 'a password needs at least 8 characters'. The five findings are two minors that make a documented cold start unreproducible (d-01, d-02), one minor performance-shape finding already gated by O5 (d-03), and two cosmetics (d-04, d-05). Held below 90 because d-01 and d-02 are real reproducibility defects that broke the documented entrypoint on first run, not nits.

O3.anchorsCited: The 90 anchor: 'every probe correctly denied, including asset access after view-once/delete.' Scored just under it for probe provenance, not for lane behaviour.
O3.justification: No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so O3 rests on a grader-authored sweep over every trust-boundary category the brief publishes. All were correctly denied server-side: cross-user DM history and point reads leaked nothing; a non-member send was refused NOT_MEMBER; editing, deleting and reacting to a foreign message all refused with the state intact; non-admin rename refused; global message search surfaced nothing from a chat the caller is not in; a private asset returned 404 to an outsider, 200 to a member and 401 unauthenticated; a removed member kept pre-removal history but the server stopped serving post-removal messages; a bogus token was denied. The named grader assertions add the rest of the published set: post-logout token revocation (m1-a07), expired-edit-window refusal (m4-a10), asset refusal after delete (m4-a12), view-once re-fetch refused 410 (m5-a06), server-side expiry surviving the replica and its offline search (m5-a01..a03), and digest authorization (m8-a12). Not scored 90 because these probes are not the wave's hash-committed rotated set and were written with source access, so they cannot claim the holdout set's blind coverage.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') and the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush'), placed just below 60.
O4.justification: The dimension's own subject - cold-start offline demonstrated on the native proof - produced no scoreable artifact at all. Both supplementalExternal entries (ios-simulator-m6, ios-simulator-m8) are pass:null, receipt:null, status 'not-recorded', and artifacts/m{6,8}-ios/ hold only Hermes bundle exports, which simulator.md explicitly refuses as proof. So cold-start reads, cold-start search, the view-once no-durable-cache guarantee and durable-queue-across-restart are all undemonstrated rather than merely imperfect, which is a wider gap than the 60 anchor describes. Held well above 30 because nothing observed is empty or broken and the choreography artifacts that do exist are strong on the adjacent behaviour: the M6 web segment flushed a queued offline write in order (flushMs 13389), M5 warm-offline search over synced messages passed, and M8's dual-offline convergence and receipt-advance checks both passed with no loss and no duplicates. The dimension's honesty clause is fully satisfied - README.md states plainly that the iOS artifacts 'are Hermes bundle exports, not simulator interaction proofs', and the harness status carries an explicit reason rather than a fabricated native pass.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: the invariant manifest conforms exactly (all 18 perEntityCounts identical to invariant-manifest-combined.json, scale.log sha256 b26bf1ae... matches the pinned scale-log.sha256, 27 named spot entities checked, all three checkpoint verifications pass:true, receipt audit 167157 actions / 167157 unique / 0 failures), and the replay used 4156.4 s of its 14400 s cap (28.9%), so the cap was not exhausted. Band 30 fires on 'any degradation rule fails': two frozen mid-curve degradation rules fail at the 50% checkpoint. Global message search - the 50% p95 is 16.326 ms against the 10%-to-100% interpolated ceiling of 15.193 ms (10%: 8.987 ms, 100%: 22.952 ms; ceiling = a + (z-a)*4/9). Insights - the 50% p95 is 5.007 ms against a 4.260 ms ceiling (10%: 2.286 ms, 100%: 6.727 ms). Both recomputed independently by the grader from evidence/replay-scale/verification-{10pct,50pct,final}.json and matching the lane's own builder-envelope.json, which records allBuilderChecksPass:false. Every 3x full-corpus ratio passes (deep paging 1.04, following-500 2.89, celebrity read 0.69, celebrity write 1.01, search 2.55, Insights 2.94, Trending 1.58) and no probe timed out, errored or OOMed, so the failure is the mid-curve clause alone - but the band function is first-match and does not weigh how many rules failed.
